sources.title: IDFPR — Real Estate Brokerage
sources.publisher: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation, Division of Real Estate
sources.effectiveOrRevisionDate: current page; no document revision stated
pinpoints: Real Estate Broker, Managing Broker, and Leasing Agent
sources.evidence: The current official hub links the endorsement application, candidate bulletin, provider and course forms, and the 2020/2024 mandatory curricula used by this lock.

sources.title: Real Estate License Act of 2000 — Article 5
sources.effectiveOrRevisionDate: endorsement provisions effective 2026-01-01; section scheduled to be repealed 2030-01-01
sources.evidence: The Act controls the ordinary broker and managing-broker education paths, the 2026 endorsement conditions, and continuing education.

sources.title: 68 Ill. Adm. Code Part 1450 — Real Estate License Act of 2000
sources.publisher: Illinois General Assembly, Joint Committee on Administrative Rules
sources.effectiveOrRevisionDate: relevant endorsement and education provisions amended at 49 Ill. Reg. 9512, effective 2025-07-07
sources.evidence: The current rule text controls fees, endorsement evidence, provider and instructor licensing, approved delivery, course portfolio, exams, records, reporting, renewals, and online participation controls.

sources.title: Real Estate Application for Licensure by Endorsement
pinpoints: PDF p. 2, eligibility and application instructions
sources.evidence: The form requires license certification/history from each state, URET for the 30-hour course, Illinois-law exam score, nonresident consent, fee, and sponsor card only if active status is requested.

validation.pdfTextLayer: extracted with page boundaries and revision footer

sources.title: Real Estate Education Provider License Application
sources.evidence: The form requires a $1,050 provider fee, $150 per course, Illinois authority for a foreign entity, administrative/records materials, an Illinois-licensed instructor roster, and the seven-course pre/post portfolio.

validation.pdfTextLayer: extracted with page boundaries and revision footer

sources.title: Real Estate Brokerage Pre-License/Post-License Course Application
pinpoints: PDF p. 2, course, delivery, attachment and fee fields
sources.evidence: One application is required per course. It distinguishes LMS online distance from non-LMS home study and requires the description, timed outline excluding exam time, objectives, all student materials, and an active Illinois instructor license.

validation.pdfTextLayer: extracted with page boundaries and revision footer

sources.title: 30-Hour Real Estate Broker Endorsement Course Curriculum
pinpoints: PDF p. 1, overview and Parts I-II
PDF p. 2, Part III and time totals
sources.evidence: The required outline allocates 10 hours each to licensing, practice law/rules, and disclosures, with 1,500 instructional minutes plus 300 break minutes.

validation.pdfTextLayer: extracted; total minutes reconciled to the printed totals

sources.title: 30-Hour Real Estate Managing Broker Endorsement Course Curriculum
sources.evidence: The required outline recommends 8 hours each for licensing, practice, and disclosures plus 6 hours for managing-broker topics; 1,500 instructional minutes plus 300 break minutes.

validation.pdfTextLayer: extracted; printed section hours and total minutes reconciled

sources.title: Real Estate Broker 75-Hour Pre-License Curriculum
sources.effectiveOrRevisionDate: 2020-01-01; still linked as current curriculum by IDFPR on 2026-09-04
pinpoints: PDF pp. 2-7, required topic and applied outlines
sources.evidence: The ordinary broker curriculum is 60 hours of topics plus a 15-hour applied course; the applied course must use an approved interactive delivery method.

sources.title: Real Estate Broker 45-Hour Post-License Curriculum
sources.effectiveOrRevisionDate: 2020-01-01; still linked as current curriculum by IDFPR on 2026-09-04
sources.evidence: The post-license portfolio contains three 15-hour courses, each with its own 50-question provider exam, and includes one hour of sexual-harassment prevention training.

sources.title: Real Estate Brokerage License Requirements for a Pre-License Instructor
sources.effectiveOrRevisionDate: Rev. Dec. 2022; linked by current IDFPR hub
sources.evidence: Applicants need a 75% exam score, one listed expertise route, and an approved 12-hour instructor-development program; application is through the IDFPR online portal.

sources.title: Approved Pre-License Instructor Training Programs
sources.evidence: The official registry identifies programs IDFPR presently accepts for the 12-hour instructor-training requirement.

sources.title: Illinois Real Estate Candidate Information Booklet
sources.publisher: PSI Services LLC under contract with IDFPR
sources.evidence: The bulletin documents PSI administration, endorsement education upload, scheduling, attempts, and exam lengths. Its Broker endorsement paragraph contains a title error and is not used to override the statute, rule, or form.

sources.title: Transact Business in Illinois — Foreign LLC
pinpoints: LLC, LP, LLP — Transact Business in Illinois
sources.evidence: A foreign LLC files LLC-45.5 in duplicate with a certificate of good standing from its formation state.

sources.title: LLC-45.5 Application for Admission to Transact Business
pinpoints: PDF pp. 1-2, filing requirements and items 1-14
sources.evidence: The filing fee is $150; an Illinois registered office/agent and a certificate of good standing or existence authenticated within 60 days are required.

sources.title: IDFPR Annual Disciplinary Report — Fiscal Year 2024
sources.publisher: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation
pinpoints: PDF p. 85, real estate applications and licenses granted
PDF p. 86, education provider and instructor applications
sources.evidence: FY2024 reported 4,212 broker applications and 3,972 licenses granted, 449 managing-broker applications and 421 granted, and 8 education-provider applications with 6 granted; applications and decisions need not be the same cohort.

sources.evidence: The minutes report 59,006 active brokers, 13,898 active managing brokers, 67 education providers, 254 pre-license instructors, and 398 pre-license courses as of February 2026.

sources.title: California Business and Professions Code §10131
sources.evidence: California broker authority includes transactions, leasing, and real-property-secured loan activity, but this statute does not itself establish equivalence to Illinois managing-broker status.
